name: Saint Paul the First Hermit
history: According to the life written by Saint Jerome, Paul fled into the Egyptian desert as a young man during the persecution of Decius and lived there alone in prayer for some ninety years. He is honoured as the first Christian hermit. Near the end of his life he was found by Saint Anthony, and the meeting of the two old men became a favourite subject of painters.
life: Paul was born in the Thebaid, in Upper Egypt, to a wealthy Christian family, and lost his parents at fifteen. When the persecution of Decius broke out around 250 he hid in the desert, and what began as flight became a vocation. Jerome tells that he lived in a cave beside a spring and a palm tree, which gave him food and clothing, and that for years a raven brought him half a loaf each day. When Anthony, then ninety, was led to his cave, the raven brought a whole loaf, and the two old men argued courteously over who should break it. Paul knew he was dying and sent Anthony to fetch the cloak Saint Athanasius had given him, to be buried in. Anthony returned to find him dead, kneeling as if in prayer, and two lions came out of the desert and dug his grave. Much of this may be legend, but Jerome meant to show a life given wholly to God.
prayerTo: Saint Paul, you left everything and lived for God alone in the silence of the desert. Pray for all hermits and contemplatives, and for me, that I may make a desert in my heart where God can speak, trust Him for my daily bread, and be ready, like you, when He calls me home. Amen.
penance: Eat simply today, perhaps bread and water at one meal if your health allows, and give the price of what you would have eaten to the poor.
meditation: For ninety years he waited on God in a cave, and God fed him day by day. What would it mean to trust God for today’s bread alone?
prayer: O God, Who gladden us with the annual feast of blessed Paul, Your Confessor, mercifully grant that, while honoring the anniversary of his death, we may also imitate his deeds. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
